title: Chapter 83 — Delivery, Install, Haul-Away, and Accessories
intro: The service lines as products, the operational handshake, and accessory discipline.

sections.title: Services Are Products
sections.content:
Delivery, installation, and haul-away are not fees. They are professional services that ensure the appliance is received safely, installed correctly, and the old unit is removed responsibly.

Present them as value. Explain what each service includes. Set accurate expectations about timing, process, and what the customer needs to prepare.

sections.title: Accessories Complete the Sale
sections.content:
Water filters, stacking kits, dryer vent kits, range cords, dishwasher installation kits, pedestals — these are the items customers will need but often do not think about.

Present accessories during the ticket build, not as an afterthought. The customer who leaves without a dryer vent kit will be frustrated when the installer asks where it is.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating service and accessory selling, ask:

Are services presented as professional value — or hidden fees?
Are accessories included in the initial ticket — or forgotten?
Does the customer leave with everything they need for a successful installation?
